## Why

Parity rows 1.5 and 1.3 and gap 14 (docs/orchestrator-parity.md in the s165 worktree). The outer session writes a thin spec: it fills Why, Files, Failing tests, Implement and Check, traces the failing tests to files and fixes the Files list (`slicer edit`). ork cannot. Its spec-check role is read-only and only asks questions (`internal/roles/prompts/spec-check.md`, `docs/design.md:661-689`). The one slicer edit ork makes is appending `Owner decisions` to Implement (`internal/engine/speccheck.go:373-374`, `internal/slicercli/write.go:236-247`).

Owner decision 2026-10-29 (orchestrator-parity.md, Owner decisions): v1.1, not v1.0.

Conflict with a decided record: `adj check scope.v1` is `decided` (adj 1, 2026-10-18): "Roadmap and decision editing wait for a later version" (`docs/dashboard.md:3-5`, `:1330`). Editing a slice's spec sections is roadmap editing. adj 11 (`ui.slicer-tui`, decided "both" on 2026-10-20) puts common edits in ork and the rest in `slicer tui`, so the direction is allowed, but no record lifts `scope.v1`. The first step of this slice is therefore an owner decision, and no code starts before it. Agents never run `adj reject` or `adj supersede`.

Design (*proposed*, only after that decision): a read-only role with its own prompt (`spec-draft.md`, ork's text) proposes section text for one slice, in the project checkout, under the same read-only fingerprint as the spec check (`role.readonly-fingerprint`). ork writes nothing until the owner approves each section. An approved section is applied with `slicer edit ID --section NAME --text ... --render` (replace), after ork re-checks that the spec has not changed since the proposal (the spec fingerprint of the spec check). The role gets the failing-tests-to-files trace as a rule of its prompt; ork checks that every path it proposes for Files exists.

## Failing tests

- TestSpecDraftReportParsesOneBlockPerSection (engine): `## Section NAME` blocks parse; an unknown section name, a missing block or a report without the Owner needed ending is a shape error.
- TestSpecDraftRoleIsReadOnly (daemon): the checkout changing during the role's run fails the draft and keeps no proposal.
- TestSpecDraftWritesNothingBeforeApproval (daemon): after a draft, no `slicer edit` call has been made.
- TestSpecDraftApprovalRunsSlicerEditPerSection (daemon): approving two of three sections makes two `slicer edit ID --section NAME --text ... --render` calls and none for the third.
- TestSpecDraftRefusesAChangedSpec (daemon): approval after the item's spec fingerprint changed is `refused`, no edit.
- TestSpecDraftRefusesAFilesPathThatDoesNotExist (engine): a Files line naming a path that is not in the checkout is reported to the owner with the section.
- TestSpecDraftViewShowsOldAndNewText (tui): the view shows the current section and the proposal, and `y` asks with the exact command.
- TestSpecDraftSurvivesNoDaemonConnection (tui): without a daemon the key shows `No daemon connection; action unavailable`.

## Implement

UI slice: UI pass (r14). v1.1. Step 1 is an owner decision; do not start step 2 before it is decided.
1. Owner decision (adj, key proposed `scope.spec-drafting`): may ork edit slice spec sections? The owner decides and, if yes, supersedes or amends `scope.v1` in adj; then update `dashboard.md:3-8`, `:1330` and `PROJECT.md:109` (it says `ui.slicer-tui` is open; adj 11 says decided "both").
2. Tests first (above), then the prompt `spec-draft.md` and its entry in `roles.go` (see `roles_test.go` for the prompt checks).
3. `internal/engine/specdraft.go`: report parser and the Files existence check. `internal/daemon/specdraft.go`: job modelled on `specCheck` (`speccheck.go:130`), methods `spec.draft` and `spec.draft-apply` (*proposed*); fingerprint guard via `engine.SpecFingerprint`.
4. `internal/slicercli/write.go`: `EditReplace` beside `EditAppend` (:239), flags `--section NAME --text TEXT --render --json --lean`.
5. TUI: a key in the Roadmap item pane (`internal/tui/roadmap.go`) opens the draft view.
Open: (1) Is spec editing in ork allowed at all (the decision above), or does it stay in `slicer tui` (adj 11)? (2) Which matrix row runs the draft: the spec-check row (u11, default, no slicer change) or a new rule "Spec draft row (rNN)" the owner adds with `slicer relay-roles rule-add`. (3) Whether the role may fill an empty slice from the title alone (default: only sections that already have text or a Why from a finding). (4) A CLI form, `ork spec draft PROJECT ID` (default: none).
